question.text: As per SEBI's mutual fund categorization, large-cap companies are those ranked in terms of full market capitalization in the list prepared by AMFI as:

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI defines large-cap companies as those ranked 1st to 100th by full market capitalization in the AMFI list. Mid-cap companies are ranked 101st to 250th, and small-cap companies are ranked 251st onwards. The Trap: 250 is the lower boundary of the mid-cap band (101 to 250), not the large-cap cut-off; 1 to 100 is what defines large-cap. Note: These rank-based market-cap definitions drive scheme categorization across large-cap, mid-cap, and small-cap funds.
